opening.argument: The presentation is structured as beginner education about Binance Earn and related cryptocurrency features. It identifies itself as a guide to “Binance passive income” and explains that the material is intended for beginners who want tutorials with everything explained. The discussion describes rewards from holding crypto or stablecoins, explains staking and liquidity farming, and gives operational instructions, including, “All we do, we click subscribe.” It also addresses risk rather than presenting returns as guaranteed, warning that higher rates involve additional risks and reporting that liquidity farming “hasn't been that successful” for the speaker. The Binance referral link and disclosed reward or trading-fee percentage are openly identified, while the stated source of some rewards is trading fees from Binance users. These facts establish an instructional demonstration with disclosed promotion and risk discussion, not a demonstrated deceptive promise or fraudulent money or data flow.

citations.quote: Welcome to my guide on Binance passive income.
They are for beginners in crypto, but I feel like there are a lot of beginners in crypto and I want them to have a safe place where they can watch tutorials and get everything explained to them.
Be aware that, usually if you can get a higher rate, there are other risks involved!
I've tried it for over one year now and it's not been that successful.
There will, of course, be links to Binance down below, with a referral link where I get a small reward or a small percentage of the trading fees if you trade on Binance.
